why: The statement asks for a precise determination of every congruent number, so any result deciding a family of n (Heegner, Monsky, Tian, TYZ, Das-Mondal, Xu, the OpenAI low-Selmer-corank converse) is a case, while proportion results (Smith 2016/2017, Burungale-Tian 50%) are bounds. Tunnell's unconditional forward direction decides non-congruence wherever the counts differ, so it is a case rather than a mere reduction. Whole-problem BSD proof claims (Matnyak, Prastaro, Iran formula, Lippy) carry several F10 signals together and are set aside. Chen-Ma-Du decides only already-known n and is none; the trillion computation and Deshpande are instances; theta- and pi/3-congruent and rank records are variants. The OpenAI rows are scored generated from the README's statement that results were obtained by the internal model; the record shows no human mathematical authorship. Close calls: Burungale-Tian and Das-Mondal 8k+3 marked digested on stated journal acceptance (Annals, J. Algebra) not independently confirmed; OpenAI events doubtful rather than knocked down because the GitHub issue's author themselves says it is not a disproof.
doubts: openai-bsd-2026 and openai-math-002 describe the same family (002), and openai-2-converse-2026 / openai-goldfeld-2026 overlap openai-math-006; they are scored separately but are not independent results. The OpenAI AI attribution rests on a general README sentence not naming these manuscripts. The congruent-number consequence of the OpenAI theorems is the researcher's deduction. Smith 2016 'digested' could be argued from Goldfeld's prize write-up, but that was a snippet only.
